newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares up, traders expect market breather.
newsitem.headline: German shares up, traders expect market breather.

text.p: German shares forged strongly ahead in electronic share trade on Friday, recouping Thursday's losses, but dealers expected the market to take a breather in coming weeks and allow fundamental factors to catch up.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index stood at 2,855.60 points at 1447 GMT, up 35.58 points or around one-and-a-quarter percent, making up for Thursday's drop.

"The market is going to stay volatile next week, but I would stick with sideways volatility. Fundamentals have to catch up with the market after the bull-run of recent weeks," said one Frankfurt trader.
One of the main factors behind Friday's recovery was the fact that Wall Street had a late rally on Thursday.

"People were happy that Wall Street didn't go badly," said the trader. Wall Street opened higher on Friday afternoon, up over half a percentage point at 6,481.75 points early on, which continued to support the IBIS DAX index.

The other main factor underpinning the market was the strength of the debt market, with Bunds firming throughout the afternoon, and the dollar, which continued to strengthen against the mark over the day, to stand at 1.5545/50 marks later on.

For next week, traders were expecting the market to find support at around 2,800 points, with resistance pegged at around 2,860 points, and did not rule out the possibility of 30-point fluctuations every day.

Most market players would be back from holiday by next week. Looking at individual sectors, dealers were forecasting a possible move out of the chemical sector into cyclical stocks, such as engineering stocks or construction stocks.
Dealers said domestic fund managers were helping underpin the market as they bought up German blue-chips in a bid to increase their German equity weightings early in the year.
Chemical stocks profited from the strengthening dollar, with Bayer AG up 66 pfennigs at 61.81 marks, BASF AG up 1.64 marks at 58.63 marks and Hoechst AG up 79 pfennigs at 70.51 marks.
The financial sector also saw a lot of what volume there was in a relatively thin market, particularly the three major banks.
Commerzbank AG was up 1.59 marks at 39.85 marks, Deutsche Bank AG was up 45 pfennigs at 71.50 marks and Dresdner Bank AG was up 87 pfennigs at 45.48 marks.
